newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Guinness, GrandMet announce merger.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Guinness, GrandMet announce merger.

text.p: Britain's Guinness Plc and Grand Metropolitan Plc on Monday announced they would merge to form a new company which would be a major new force in international food and drinks.

The companies said the new company, called GMG Brands, would deliver significant cost savings. Shareholders in GrandMet, which owns Burger King and food group Pillsbury, along with drinks interests, will own 52.7 percent of the new company.

On Friday's share price, the combined value of the group was 20.61 billion pounds ($33.5 billion), making it the seventh largest food and drinks company worldwide and Britain's eighth largest quoted company.

The merger will also create the world's leading branded spirits and wine company with combined spirits sales of over 100 million cases, bringing together brands like GrandMet-owned Smirnoff vodka and Cinzano with Guinness owned Johnnie Walker whisky and Gordon's gin.
The deal includes a capital repayment to shareholders of not less than 60 pence per share, worth some 2.4 billion pounds ($3.9 billion).

"We have brought together two highly successful British-based companies which own some of the world's leading consumer brands, creating a powerful group comprising four world class branded businesses," said George Bull, GrandMet chairman.
GMG Brands' four divisions will be United Distillers and Vintners, the combined spirits and wines business, Pillsbury, Burger King and Guinness Brewing Worldwide.

The merger gives Guinness an increased interest in North America through GrandMet's food subsidiary Pillsbury and Burger King, while GrandMet shareholders will benefit from Guinness spirits' business in emerging markets.
Pillsbury brands include Green Giant vegetables and Haagen-Dazs ice cream and Progresso soups.
Guinness also brews Guinness stout, one of the world's most widely distributed beers, brewed in 50 countries and sold in about 150.

Guinness shareholders will keep their shares in Guinness, to be renamed GMG Brands, while GrandMet shareholders will get one new GMG Brands share for every GrandMet share held. GrandMet shareholders will hold about 52.7 percent and Guinness shareholders the remainder of the merged company.
